card.summary: Lets an agent hand off long or batched work and answer when it finishes, instead of keeping a chat open.
card.example: A person asks the agent to check fifty applications. The agent queues them, the work runs in the background, and the results are ready when the person comes back.
cost: Billed by the hour for the queue service that is running, and by the number of messages handled on some tiers.
Long jobs still use the model, so the cost of each job doesn't change. Only the waiting does.
needs: A rule for how long a job may run, how often it may retry, and what happens when it keeps failing.
A named person who owns jobs that fail or sit unfinished.
card.safety: Each job would hold what a person asked and what the agent found, so it needs the same retention and deletion rules as conversation memory. A finished job is only shown to the person who started it, and failed jobs never retry forever.
card.billing: Per hour by tier, plus per message on the lower tiers.
card.note: The queue must be private, with no public network access, so building it needs its own approval first.
